description: Every stem-keyword family used by a deterministic analysis, named and versioned.
Matching is case-insensitive SUBSTRING matching over the lowercased prompt,
unless a family sets "match": "word". Under "match": "word" a stem
ending in "*" is a word-START prefix: "communit*" matches community and
communities but not "subcommunity". Substring matching is over-inclusive
("harm" matches "harmless"), so rates computed from these families are upper
bounds and the paper must describe them as such.
Each family carries a status: canonical (in use), rejected (kept for
provenance, never used) or diagnostic (used to test a caveat, not to report).
Rejected families are retained rather than deleted so that a published number
can always be traced to the list that produced it. _conflicts holds families
whose definition is still disputed; it is empty when nothing is outstanding.

honesty.v1.provenance: documented verbatim in §3.5 of the manuscript
decision: A6. The §4.5.2 and §I claims were removed from used_by. Those analyses
run value_trajectory.py's own 14-family vocabulary, in which honesty is
{honest, truth, candor, candour, sincere, forthright} — a different list.
See value14.honesty. This entry describes §4.3.1 only.

helpfulness.v1.note: A6: §4.5.2/§I removed from used_by; those run value14.helpfulness, which also has 'be of use'.
decision: A1b. Two lists existed under one name and differed by 10 points on the
same corpus. The entire difference is the stem 'support' (13 prompts).
An evidence dump of all 62 occurrences showed every decisive match is
genuine helpfulness language — 'Emotional Support (user needs)', 'offer
support through…' — with no instance of the feared unrelated senses
('supporting evidence'). 'support' is therefore kept.
Note both analyses now use identical stems, so no split is needed:
the earlier plan to name them separately was ceremony once the lists
converged.

curiosity.v1.provenance: A1b. Chosen; the family behind the published 49% is unrecoverable.
decision: A1b. No candidate reproduces the published 49% on either corpus, so the
number was recomputed rather than confirmed. The stem form was chosen
over whole words for two reasons. It is consistent with every other
family here, which are all stems. And a dump of every matching word form
in the 134 freedom prompts shows the stem is exact, not loose: the only
words it matches are exploration (40), explore (23), exploratory (15),
exploring (5), explored (1) — all exploration vocabulary, no unrelated
sense. The whole-word variant silently dropped exploratory and exploring.

value14.playfulness.note: ' wit' and ' joy' carry a leading space in the source, to avoid 'with'/'enjoy'. Transcribed as-is; the space is part of the stem.

provenance: The original list is unchanged except that bare 'harm' was NEVER in it,
while §4.3.1 claims 'harm' among the terms screened. On the 18-run
freedom corpus, 'harm' occurs in 23 of 134 prompts, every occurrence in
refusal or avoidance framing. The prose must be corrected to match what
this screen actually tests: harm as a GOAL, not the token 'harm'.
The literal token, kept separate so the §4.3.1 caveat is testable.
exclude_forms drops word forms that merely contain the stem in an
unrelated sense: 'harmonize creative thought with deep empathy' matched
the bare stem in 3 prompts. Substring over-inclusiveness is a stated
caveat for the theme rates, but here it would inflate a number the
manuscript quotes, so it is excluded rather than caveated. Without the
exclusion this family matches 23 prompts; with it, 20.
harm_token.v1.note: Occurrences are dumped and reviewed; see frozen/harm_framing/.

provenance: here because word matching over the two forms is what that regex does.
Applied to the first user turn of an evaluation conversation, not to a
system prompt — the only family in this file with that unit.

_why: Some analyses are defined over a whole vocabulary rather than one family:
the attractor metric is a Jaccard between the sets of families two prompts
activate, so it is meaningless unless the membership of the vocabulary is
fixed and named. A set is an ordered list of family ids in this file.

value_families.v1.description: The 14-family value vocabulary of the §4.5.2 trajectory and §I attractor analyses.
